final_candidates.decision_summary: D473 is a membrane-domain acidic residue corresponding to the conserved OCT substrate-interaction carboxylate. Neutralizing this charge is strongly expected to abolish organic-cation transport while retaining the transmembrane scaffold.

R232 lies within the pore-associated GSGSRRT region and removing its positive charge should strongly impair cation translocation. The hydrophobic leucine replacement is intended to reduce folding disruption relative to more radical substitutions.

D356 is a membrane-embedded acidic residue plausibly involved in substrate recognition or translocation. Aspartate-to-alanine neutralization offers a conservative route to loss of transport while limiting secondary effects on helix packing.

stop_reason.detail: The maximum agent-round budget has been reached, so the final top three are reported from the available mechanistic reasoning.

history.rationale: Asp in TM11 (C472-D473) corresponds to the conserved, transport-critical carboxylate in the OCT substrate-binding cavity (homolog of D475 implicated in cation binding); neutralization typically abolishes transport while the transporter still folds and traffics.

Conserved acidic residue in TM11 matching the canonical OCT substrate-binding carboxylate; charge neutralization is the most mechanistically grounded way to abolish cation transport while retaining fold.
Arg within the GSGSRRT motif of TM4; basic residues at this position line the substrate translocation pore, and charge removal is known to eliminate cation transport in OCTs.
Arg in the TM4 GSGSRRT pore-lining motif; removing a basic charge from the translocation pathway is a well-supported loss-of-transport strategy in OCTs.

Asp in TM7 (T355-D356) sits in the membrane domain; acidic residues in OCT TM helices contribute to substrate interaction, and neutralization is a plausible transport-null mutation with minimal folding impact.
Membrane-embedded Asp in TM7 plausibly contributing to substrate interaction; conservative Asp→Ala neutralization should impair transport without destabilizing the helix.

C61 forms the large extracellular loop disulfide (C49-C61) required for proper OCT1 function; removing one cysteine disrupts loop conformation and transport while the transmembrane scaffold remains expressed.
Breaks the C49–C61 extracellular disulfide needed for OCT1 function, but carries a modest risk of reduced surface abundance, so kept below the TM charge mutants.
Asp in the central membrane region (I396-D397-R398) adjacent to the DR(V)GRI motif lining the translocation path; neutralization is a reasonable transport-ablation hypothesis.
Asp adjacent to the DR(V)GRI translocation-path motif; plausible transport-ablation candidate but with weaker mechanistic support than the top three.
